Exercise A

Structure and linking

A clear email has a subject line, a greeting, a reason, a request and a closing. Linking words show how your ideas connect. Choose the best option for each gap.

Before you start — optional, not marked
This is just to get you thinking. You can leave it empty and it does not count towards your score.
Part 1: An email to a landlord

Subject: 1

Dear Mr Evans,

The heating has been broken since Monday, 2 the flat is very cold. I have already called the helpline, 3 nobody has come yet.

Could you please send someone 4 Friday? I look forward 5 hearing from you.

Kind regards,
Sam Brown

Part 2: Choose the best linking word

6. I would like to move my seminar group, 6 we have a clash with another class.

7. The room is free on Monday. 7, it is booked all day on Tuesday.

8. I missed the first session. 8, could you send me the slides?

9. Please find the form 9 to this email.

10. I apologise for any 10.

Exercise B

Write your email

Write on your own, 15 minutes. Choose a real or realistic problem. Use all five parts: subject line, greeting, reason, request and closing. Do not use translation software.

Word count: 0 (aim for 100–130)

Say why you are writing, ask for one clear thing, give any dates or details, and finish politely. Use at least two linking words.

Exercise C

Check a partner's email

Send your email to a partner in the chat and read theirs. Find the five parts, then write your feedback here. Be specific and kind.

Do not write your partner's name. Say “your email”.
